evidence_summary: Tone Machines identifies LIMMCO as a wholesale/distribution company based in Hicksville, New York and describes Bob Seidman as a major connection among Applied, Nomad, Kimberly, UMI, Guild, Goya and related brands. This supports LIMMCO as a network/distribution node rather than a single pedal factory.

Gearphoria's UMI history states that Richard Soloway first made amplifiers for Gracin's Music in Freeport, New York before UMI began making pedals. This anchors a genuine UMI-Gracin's business relationship but does not make Gracin's a UMI factory label.

Tone Machines places Gracin's Fubar among East Coast Fuzz examples and notes that the 3-knob Gracin's form is a late-stage family variant. Similar 94047-marked transistors and construction details support shared production origin but not a named factory.

Effects Database explicitly lists Gracin's & Towne Wa & Volume as made by Foxx/fOXX. This is independent evidence that the Gracin's label appeared on products made by a different manufacturer from the East Coast Fuzz and UMI branches.

Tone Machines identifies Nomad Banshee Fuzz as an Applied Audio product distributed by LIMMCO and also notes that exact manufacturing dates remain uncertain. This reinforces Nomad as a LIMMCO-associated house brand with supplier-specific product states.
Effects Database catalogs a Nomad Tone Booster as Nomad by UMI. This is model-specific evidence and must not be generalized to the whole Nomad brand.

Tone Machines documents a rare Nomad Super Fuzz with an early germanium Fuzzrite-type circuit and original-looking Nomad markings, but finds no evidence tying it to the later LIMMCO/Applied Nomad products or proving a Mosrite transaction. The supplier remains unresolved.

physical_builder_candidate: multiple period suppliers: LIMMCO, Applied, later UMI
evidence_summary: Effects Database separates Kimberly fuzz production into v1 by LIMMCO and v2 by Applied, while Tone Machines documents a later UMI redesign/production phase. Kimberly therefore provides a model-level example of LIMMCO moving from in-house manufacture into outside suppliers and later UMI production.

The surviving evidence spans at least three distinct Gracin's product supply chains: an East Coast Fuzz family fuzz, a UMI amplifier customer relationship, and a Foxx-made Gracin's & Towne Wa & Volume. The label therefore cannot be used as a physical-builder proxy.
